evidence: Every route matched by a declared route-auth contract rule reaches an authentication or authorization check in its call path at the scanned commit, and every declared rule matches at least one route the code graph found
expected_output: One row per (declared rule, matched route): rule_id, matched, route, file, line, auth_reached, auth_symbol, call_path, call_path_resolutions — plus a matched:false row for any rule whose pattern matched no route

assertions.description: Every route matched by a declared route-auth rule reaches an authentication check in its call path (under-approximate calls/handles walk over graph.db).
Every declared route-auth rule matches at least one route the graph found — a rule that matches nothing is checking nothing, and a mistyped pattern must fail rather than pass.

notes: L1: the contract gate promotes route-auth-coverage's heuristic to declared intent. route-auth-coverage observes every route against a name pattern; this recipe checks only the routes the repo's own rampscan.config.json contract says MUST pass, with the same under-approximate walk (calls/handles edges only — a positive auth claim needs a real chain). The rules evaluated ride the bundle's basis as canonical JSON and are keyed into evidence identity, so editing a rule re-keys the evidence. A repo with no contract stays honestly unevidenced with a stated skip; a repo whose graph found no routes stays unevidenced too. Empty-set discipline — Skip plus negative witness: no contract, no declared route rule or no route the extractor saw and the collector skips with a stated reason; when it does run, every declared rule contributes at least one row — its matched routes, or the `matched: false` row saying the pattern matches nothing — so an empty observation set could only mean nothing was searched.

plain.checks: Reads the architecture contract the repository declares in its rampscan.config.json — which routes must require an authenticated caller — and follows each matching route's call path through the code to see whether an authentication check actually sits on the way in.
plain.violation: The code and the repository's own declared intent disagree: a route the contract says must check identity serves requests without checking any. A declared rule that matches no route at all also fails, because a mistyped pattern would otherwise quietly waive the very rule it meant to state.
plain.fix: Add the check to the route's handler or to middleware mounted in front of it — or, if the intent genuinely changed, amend the contract in rampscan.config.json, where the change is reviewed like any other. A rule that matches nothing needs its route pattern corrected.
